articles.title: WHO scales up Ebola readiness in 22 countries across three continents

events.summary: The World Health Organization is stepping up Ebola preparedness across 22 countries spanning Africa, Asia, and Europe. The agency highlighted increased risk driven by regional conflict and displacement affecting millions of people.
events.why: Cross-continental containment measures are essential to stop high-fatality pathogens from spreading across fragile borders.

articles.title: Could your brain data be used against you? UN calls for limits on neurotechnology

events.summary: A UN report warns that rapid developments in neurotechnology are outpacing human rights legislation. The report cautions that brain data collected by consumer wellness gadgets or gaming headsets could potentially be used as evidence in court.
events.why: Unregulated commercial collection of neural data poses fundamental risks to personal privacy and civil liberties.

articles.title: Iran war live: IRGC says supertanker hit naval mine in Hormuz, catches fire

events.summary: An oil supertanker caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after striking a naval mine. The incident was reported directly by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
events.why: Naval mine strikes against supertankers in vital straits pose severe risks of broader military escalation and maritime transit shutdown.

articles.title: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
Brazil’s Amazon deforestation hits lowest level on record
Brazil: Amazon deforestation lowest in nearly 40 years
Brazilian Amazon deforestation falls to lowest on record as pivotal vote looms

events.summary: Brazil has recorded a record drop in Amazon deforestation, reaching its lowest level in nearly 40 years. Deforestation had previously expanded under former president Jair Bolsonaro, threatening the rainforest's capacity as a buffer against climate change.
events.why: Preserving the Amazon is critical for global carbon sequestration and climate change mitigation.

articles.title: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels amid rampant rights violations

events.summary: Acute hunger and malnutrition in Afghanistan have reached record highs, with 15.9 million individuals facing acute food insecurity. A global hunger monitor report indicated that conditions are anticipated to deteriorate further in upcoming months.
events.why: Mass starvation and institutional paralysis threaten the survival of millions of Afghan civilians.

articles.title: WHO urges vigilance after Kenya confirms second Ebola case

events.summary: The World Health Organization is supporting containment efforts in Kenya following a second confirmed case of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus. The update was confirmed by the UN agency's representative in the country.
events.why: Unchecked spread of the Ebola virus carries high mortality rates and presents a severe public health containment challenge.

articles.title: WHO urges faster action to end lead exposure which kills 3.5 million annually

events.summary: The World Health Organization urged countries to accelerate measures against lead exposure, which affects hundreds of millions of children. The agency estimates lead exposure causes more than 3.5 million deaths globally every year.
events.why: Lead poisoning is a major global health hazard causing millions of preventable deaths and irreversible neurological harm in children.

articles.title: Ship attack reports near Hormuz reach record high as oil exports slow

events.summary: Attacks on maritime vessels near the Strait of Hormuz reached record highs, with 12 ships struck within a single week. The incidents have led to a slowdown in oil exports according to UK maritime data analyzed by the BBC.
events.why: Maritime violence around critical energy transit corridors threatens international oil trade flows and increases global economic volatility.

articles.title: Security Council LIVE: Sudan’s war spreads as drones and hunger take a deadly toll

events.summary: The UN Security Council convened to address Sudan's hunger and displacement crisis as drone strikes and famine expand across Darfur, Kordofan, and other regions. Ambassadors intend to push for an immediate ceasefire, weapon supply halts, and safe humanitarian access.
events.why: Sudan represents the world's largest hunger and displacement crisis, carrying massive regional instability risks.

articles.title: Gaza: 340 children killed despite ceasefire agreement - UNICEF

events.summary: Over 340 children have been killed and hundreds injured in Gaza roughly one year after a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas fighters, according to UNICEF.
events.why: Persistent casualties undermine ceasefire terms and reflect sustained humanitarian devastation for civilians.

articles.title: Trump waives several Russia sanctions as new US law takes effect
Trump puts new Russia sanctions on hold

events.summary: Donald Trump has waived several sanctions against Russia under a newly enacted U.S. law meant to penalize Moscow for the war in Ukraine. Trump asserted that portions of the legislation run contrary to U.S. national interests.
events.why: Waiving statutory sanctions alters U.S. foreign policy leverage and impacts the economic pressure exerted on Russia.

articles.title: How prepared is Kenya for an Ebola outbreak?

events.summary: Kenya has reported its first two confirmed cases of Ebola, prompting questions regarding border controls and preparedness. The Health Ministry has stated there is currently no need for panic.
events.why: The entry of a highly lethal virus into a new geographic area carries high public health risks and demands rapid containment.

articles.title: Trump denies limiting Ukraine access to Starlink network

events.summary: Donald Trump denied limiting Ukraine's access to the Starlink network. Speed curbs reportedly hampered Ukraine's defense against deadly Russian attacks on Tuesday night.
events.why: Restrictions on critical battlefield communications directly affect front-line survival, defense capabilities, and territorial integrity in the Ukraine war.

articles.title: The world is waging a ‘war on nature’ as progress on biodiversity targets lags

events.summary: A UN report warns that fewer than half of national targets to protect global ecosystems, plants, and animals are on track. The warning comes shortly before countries assemble in Yerevan, Armenia, for the COP17 biodiversity conference.
events.why: Widespread failure to meet conservation goals accelerates permanent global species extinction and ecological collapse.

articles.title: Ukraine: Civilian casualty rates among ‘deadliest’ in years, as energy attacks intensify

events.summary: UN human rights monitors reported that civilian casualties in Ukraine remain at record levels following intensified Russian attacks in September. The rate of harm in 2026 significantly exceeds figures from previous years alongside escalated strikes on energy infrastructure.
events.why: Intensifying attacks on civilians and basic energy systems present severe humanitarian and systemic survival risks.

articles.title: Inside Ukrainian offensive pushing Russia back - with Starlink playing a key role

events.summary: Ukrainian forces have regained territory in the Donbas during Operation Vivaldi, utilizing Starlink systems. Strategic momentum remains affected by strained relations with President Trump.
events.why: Territorial shifts in the Donbas and shifts in allied technological and political support directly alter the trajectory of the war.

articles.title: They fled Russia, but the West sent them back

events.summary: Deportations of anti-government Russian activists from the EU and the US have risen sharply over the past year. These individuals were forcibly returned despite having sought refuge from Russia.
events.why: Forced repatriations of political dissidents to an authoritarian state present grave threats to asylum protections and human rights standards.

articles.title: Nicolás Maduro tells New York court new torture allegations are ‘false’

events.summary: Nicolás Maduro appeared in a New York court, claiming torture allegations in a revised drug trafficking indictment are false. The rewritten indictment accuses him and his wife of leading a campaign of torture.
events.why: The prosecution of a foreign head of state in a US court carries major implications for international law and diplomatic precedents.

articles.title: Guterres urges faster action and financing to stop biodiversity loss

events.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres urged governments, businesses, and communities to hasten biodiversity protection and secure financing. The appeal highlights the need to preserve all life on Earth for future generations.
events.why: Halting ecological degradation requires unprecedented mobilization of international environmental financing.

articles.title: Meta employees say Lula’s accounts restricted in Brazil election: Report

events.summary: Leaked internal messages from Meta employees indicate the platform restricted candidate Lula's accounts during Brazil's election while recommending rival Jair Bolsonaro's profile and WhatsApp channel.
events.why: Selective platform restrictions on presidential candidates during national elections threaten democratic fairness and institutional trust.

articles.title: AI, green energy and economic transitions risk leaving vulnerable communities behind, UN warns

events.summary: A UN report warns that transitions in AI, digital technology, renewable energy, and demographics are reshaping global economies while threatening to worsen inequalities. The report stresses that vulnerable communities are at severe risk of being left behind.
events.why: Structural global economic shifts without adequate social protections could permanently deepen international wealth disparities.

articles.title: At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan
Pakistan school roof collapse kills at least 34 children and teacher

events.summary: A school roof collapsed through three classrooms in Pakistan, burying children under rubble. At least 33 to 34 pupils and a teacher were killed in the incident.
events.why: A catastrophic structural failure resulting in mass casualties highlights severe infrastructure and building safety risks.

articles.title: Houthi missile attack on Yemeni presidential palace kills five, minister says
Houthi missiles strike Yemen presidential palace, killing five

events.summary: A Houthi ballistic missile strike on Yemen's al-Maashiq presidential palace killed five individuals. Yemen's information minister stated that the prime minister and other cabinet members were unhurt.
events.why: Direct strikes targeting top governmental leadership heighten volatility in Yemen's protracted civil conflict.

articles.title: As disasters mount, next UN climate summit faces a test of trust

events.summary: Representatives of three consecutive UN climate summit presidencies met ahead of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye. The discussions focused on how to restore trust in global climate action amid intensifying warming-related disasters.
events.why: International climate negotiations dictate global commitments and funding for carbon emissions reductions.

articles.title: Watch: What does Starlink have to do with the Ukraine-Russia war?

events.summary: Ukraine's president informed Elon Musk that restricting access to the Starlink satellite system results in lost lives. The technology plays an active role in the Ukraine-Russia conflict.
events.why: Private satellite infrastructure access directly determines communication reliability and operational safety on active frontlines.

articles.title: EU summit to focus on China, Ukraine and bloc budget

events.summary: EU leaders are meeting in Brussels to address the bloc's trade deficit with China, the war in Ukraine, and the next EU budget. The discussions occur ahead of upcoming major elections.
events.why: Decisions on the EU budget and China trade policy influence economic stability and geopolitical alignment across Europe.

articles.title: Trump calls off livestream of Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad

events.summary: Donald Trump canceled plans to livestream the execution by firing squad of Fort Hood attacker Nidal Hasan. This marks the first US military execution carried out in more than 60 years.
events.why: It marks the resumption of US military capital punishment after six decades, accompanied by unprecedented public broadcast debate.

articles.title: Toxic algorithms wouldn't let them go - now Australia wants an off switch

events.summary: Australia has proposed legislation to mandate an 'off switch' on social media platforms. This regulation would compel platforms to allow users to disable algorithmic recommendations.
events.why: Mandatory user controls on recommendation engines would set a major legal precedent for global digital platform regulation.

articles.title: Ukraine: Critical health supplies destroyed in ongoing Russian attacks

events.summary: Russian attacks across Ukraine have caused significant healthcare disruptions and destroyed over $1.5 million in UN medical supplies across four warehouse strikes since July. The ongoing strikes continue to impact health infrastructure nationwide.
events.why: Targeting medical supply depots critically degrades emergency healthcare delivery to populations in conflict zones.

articles.title: Ukraine president targets Trump, Putin at EU summit

events.summary: President Zelenskyy addressed an EU summit, warning that Russia's ambitions reach past eastern Ukraine. He stated that Russian drone attacks pose a threat to NATO.
events.why: It highlights diplomatic efforts to frame the Ukrainian defense directly within broader NATO and European security frameworks.

articles.title: Future of western security is at stake in Yemen civil war, says country’s former PM

events.summary: Yemen's former prime minister Maeen Abdulmalik Saeed warned that Houthi drone capabilities threaten Western security. He highlighted that a besieged southwestern city faces fuel and food shortages as it prepares for a potential Houthi breakthrough.
events.why: Persistent civil conflict and drone proliferation in Yemen threaten critical regional stability and trade routes.

articles.title: Oregon school shooter was former special needs student, police say
Shooter in fatal Bend, Oregon, school shooting was former student there

events.summary: A former student killed four people during a school shooting in Bend, Oregon. A teacher confronted the teenage shooter before a parent shot and killed him.
events.why: A fatal school shooting resulting in multiple deaths impacts community safety and public security protocols.

articles.title: Oregon teacher fought school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'

events.summary: Police stated a 16-year-old former student targeted a special educational needs classroom at an Oregon primary school. A teacher fought the attacker before an armed parent shot the suspect multiple times.
events.why: Details on the specific classroom targeting and civilian intervention provide crucial facts on the Oregon school shooting.

articles.title: US records 4,410 measles cases as outbreak grows

events.summary: The US has recorded 4,410 measles cases and 451 hospitalisations nationwide. The CDC and health officials are expanding vaccination efforts to combat the growing outbreak.
events.why: A significant outbreak of a highly contagious, preventable disease stresses public health systems and indicates gaps in herd immunity.

articles.title: Security Council LIVE: Deaths, demolitions spike in Gaza, West Bank

events.summary: The UN Security Council convened an open debate to address escalating lethal strikes, demolitions, and violence in Gaza and the West Bank. The meeting focused specifically on conditions across the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
events.why: Formal Security Council debates reflect international diplomatic pressure over worsening humanitarian crises and territorial destruction.

articles.title: A thousand slogans echoed here - but it could be the end for iconic Delhi protest site

events.summary: The historic 18th-century site Jantar Mantar in Delhi has been officially denotified as a designated protest area. The site had served as a primary location for civil demonstrations for decades.
events.why: The administrative closure of a premier public demonstration space curtails historic civil protest infrastructure in the nation's capital.

articles.title: Watch: Will Ukraine get the support needed as tensions with US rise?
Ukrainian President Zelenskyy speaks at EU summit amid spat with Donald Trump
At summit, EU leaders pledge support for Ukraine's Zelenskyy
EU’s support to Ukraine matters more than ever, von der Leyen says, as US relationship sours – as it happened

events.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy addressed an EU summit in Brussels and thanked leaders ahead of meetings. The gathering occurred amid diplomatic tensions with Donald Trump and discussions over continued European aid.
events.why: European diplomatic and financial support remains vital for sustaining Ukraine's defense posture.

articles.title: Pope pictured for first time since surgery and cancer diagnosis

events.summary: The Pope was pictured for the first time following surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital and a subsequent diagnosis of lung cancer.
events.why: The health and potential succession of the leader of the global Catholic Church affects over a billion adherents and international diplomatic affairs.

articles.title: Albanian protests turn violent: What we know

events.summary: Anti-government protests led by the 'Flamingo' movement in Albania's capital, Tirana, have escalated significantly and turned violent after months of demonstrations.
events.why: Escalating civil unrest and violence in a European capital threaten national political stability.

articles.title: Hijab ban at schools in Azerbaijan: What's behind the rare wave of protests?

events.summary: Girls wearing headscarves are being turned away from schools in Azerbaijan under unwritten rules not officially mentioned in government regulations. This has sparked rare public protests involving children.
events.why: Unwritten religious dress bans impact educational access and civil liberties, triggering unusual public resistance in the country.

articles.title: Trump in Georgia falsely claims election of Jon Ossoff was illegitimate

events.summary: At a rally in north Georgia, Donald Trump again claimed the 2020 election in Georgia was fraudulent. He specifically alleged that the election of US Senator Jon Ossoff was illegitimate.
events.why: Continued public challenges to certified federal election outcomes erode institutional trust in democratic processes.

articles.title: Patients in chains rescued from suspected illegal rehab centre in South Africa

events.summary: Authorities rescued around 200 patients found in chains from an alleged illegal rehabilitation centre in South Africa. Victims were discovered in overcrowded conditions with sores covering their bodies.
events.why: The incident reveals egregious human rights abuses and lack of regulatory oversight in private mental health and addiction facilities.
